text:
MPC fell slightly today after climbing sharply over the prior three trading days. The stock's decline follows a sharp reversal in oil markets on Monday (Sept. 21), when crude dropped below $100 a barrel on diplomatic optimism around Iran—a move that undercut some of the gains refiners had enjoyed when tensions and prices were higher. Today's continued weakness reflects ongoing uncertainty: while the Strait of Hormuz situation remains a potential supply threat, markets are now pricing in the possibility of de-escalation rather than further disruption, which reduces the urgency that had driven oil and refiner stocks higher.

Refineries are running at 96.8% capacity with robust inventory levels across products, so there's no supply-side constraint supporting prices from that angle. The broader market remains genuinely unsure about oil's direction—as one analyst noted today, Wall Street admits it doesn't know where prices head next given the geopolitical variables at play. That uncertainty is reflected in oil's sideways trading and in MPC's pullback after its recent run-up.
